purpose: reader-facing explanation of the ChatGPT Data Viewer input, architecture, search, and limitations

required_facts.fact: The viewer was created after ChatGPT search failed to find an earlier course conversation and manual scrolling was ineffective.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 3-9: lost conversation, failed search, export, and resulting tool idea are described.

required_facts.fact: The ChatGPT export download was 775 MB and the ZIP was incomplete and unreadable by Windows.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 22-32: notification, file size, and corrupted archive are stated.

required_facts.fact: Claude Code extracted important content from the archive, including conversations.json of about 155 MB and chat.html of about 160 MB.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 37-42: extraction and export files are described.

required_facts.fact: The initial interface idea was a GitHub-style contribution graph with date-based conversation details.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 49: contribution graph and date interaction are specified.

required_facts.fact: Claude helped with the UI mockup and API response format, and the planned architecture used FastAPI with Vite and vanilla JavaScript.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 51-64: design and architecture planning are described.

required_facts.fact: The workflow used no tests or Test-Driven Development, and Claude managed implementation without Alexey examining the code.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 68-75: development limitations are explicit.

required_facts.fact: The first stable version took one or two iterations and about two to three hours.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 82: iteration count and total time are stated.

required_facts.fact: The backend used FastAPI, the frontend used Vite-bundled vanilla JavaScript, minsearch powered search, and one FastAPI server served the frontend.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 89-96: architecture and single-server deployment are described.

required_facts.fact: The archive contained 2,808 conversations and 45,247 messages spanning 2022-12-21 to 2026-02-06.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 100-107: usage statistics and time span are listed.

required_facts.fact: The first search found the course conversation, while caching was added after initial indexing took time.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 123-127: search result and indexing bottleneck are described.

author_attribution: Explain the historical implementation as Alexey documented it, retaining the absence of tests and the distinction between a usable tool and possible future polish.
